risk:fuel_charged.title: (Un)predictability of strong El Ni\~no events
risk:fuel_charged.our_title: The Pendulum That Forgets How to Swing
risk:fuel_charged.oneliner: Strong El Niños can vanish for decades because the climate system flips between two distinct modes of oscillation.
risk:fuel_charged.why: Adds a caveat: even in a recharge oscillator model, timing of strong El Niños can be unpredictable despite heat accumulation.

risk:peak_ahead.title: Intrinsic unpredictability of strong El Ni\~no events
risk:peak_ahead.our_title: The Pacific Ocean Pendulum: Why Strong El Niños Are Unpredictable
risk:peak_ahead.oneliner: The ocean behaves like a pendulum that sometimes swings to huge amplitudes and sometimes gets stuck in small oscillations, and the switch between these regimes cannot be predicted.
risk:peak_ahead.why: This paper finds a mechanism that can make strong El Niño events unpredictable, supporting the dashboard's caveat that past events are no guide here.

risk:peak_ahead.title: Very early warning of a moderate-to-strong El Ni\~no in 2023
risk:peak_ahead.oneliner: Two independent methods predicted the 2023 El Niño with 89% probability and estimated its strength at 1.49±0.37°C.
risk:peak_ahead.why: This early warning study forecasts a moderate-to-strong El Niño for 2023 with an 89 percent onset chance, adding an independent forecast to the event assessment.

risk:east_pacific.title: Forecasting the El Ni\~no type well before the spring predictability barrier
risk:east_pacific.our_title: El Niño type can be predicted a year before the spring barrier
risk:east_pacific.oneliner: The difference in ocean surface temperature between the western and central Pacific in December indicates whether the next El Niño will be eastern or central.
risk:east_pacific.why: Explains how a temperature difference across the equatorial Pacific can distinguish the eastern Pacific type of El Niño from the central Pacific type.

risk:east_pacific.title: Impact of natural disasters on consumer behavior: case of the 2017 El Nino phenomenon in Peru
risk:east_pacific.our_title: A City's Pulse After a Natural Disaster
risk:east_pacific.oneliner: Bank transactions from six million Peruvians reveal how the 2017 El Niño shifted shopping habits and how quickly Lima's economy bounced back.
risk:east_pacific.why: Shows how the 2017 El Niño's heavy rains and floods disrupted spending in Peru, illustrating economic harm on South America's coast.

risk:east_pacific.title: Intrinsic unpredictability of strong El Ni\~no events
risk:east_pacific.our_title: The Pacific Ocean Pendulum: Why Strong El Niños Are Unpredictable
risk:east_pacific.oneliner: The ocean behaves like a pendulum that sometimes swings to huge amplitudes and sometimes gets stuck in small oscillations, and the switch between these regimes cannot be predicted.
risk:east_pacific.why: Cautions that the strength of extreme events like those in 1982 and 1997 can switch unpredictably, limiting forecasts of harsh impacts.

risk:coupling_on.title: Modelling the coupling between ocean and atmosphere; the global signature of the El Ni\~no/La Ni\~na Southern Oscillation
risk:coupling_on.our_title: The Planet's Pulse with an Irregular Rhythm
risk:coupling_on.oneliner: Analysis of long-term El Niño index records reveals power laws and long memory that models miss.
risk:coupling_on.why: It shows how the ocean and atmosphere exchange energy, which creates El Niño's global weather signature.

risk:coupling_on.title: Intra-annual Principal Modes and Evolution Mechanism of the El Nino Southern Oscillation
risk:coupling_on.our_title: Tug-of-War in the Tropics: How Seasonal Air Oscillations Drive El Niño
risk:coupling_on.oneliner: Two dominant intra-annual modes of tropical air temperature are closely tied to the phases of El Niño and La Niña.
risk:coupling_on.why: It links large scale air temperature patterns to El Niño phases, showing how atmospheric coupling shapes the event.

risk:coupling_on.title: Impact of natural disasters on consumer behavior: case of the 2017 El Nino phenomenon in Peru
risk:coupling_on.our_title: A City's Pulse After a Natural Disaster
risk:coupling_on.oneliner: Bank transactions from six million Peruvians reveal how the 2017 El Niño shifted shopping habits and how quickly Lima's economy bounced back.
risk:coupling_on.why: It measures how the 2017 El Niño changed consumer spending in Peru, showing economic impacts far from the warm water.

risk:warmer_next_year.title: Very early warning of a moderate-to-strong El Ni\~no in 2023
risk:warmer_next_year.oneliner: Two independent methods predicted the 2023 El Niño with 89% probability and estimated its strength at 1.49±0.37°C.
risk:warmer_next_year.why: Explains that El Nino raises global temperature by about +0.2C and likely made 2024 the hottest year.

risk:warmer_next_year.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
risk:warmer_next_year.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
risk:warmer_next_year.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
risk:warmer_next_year.why: Adds caveat that 2023's warming surge was also driven by record-low sunlight reflection, not just El Nino.

risk:new_level_sst_world.title: Empirical evidence for a double step climate change in twentieth century
risk:new_level_sst_world.our_title: The Twentieth Century's Two-Step Climate Shift
risk:new_level_sst_world.oneliner: Twentieth-century warming did not proceed smoothly, but in two sharp steps, in 1925/26 and 1987/88.
risk:new_level_sst_world.why: Finds sea surface temperatures rose in sharp persistent steps in 1925/26 and 1987/88 rather than smooth or temporary spikes.

risk:new_level_sst_world.title: Persistence without Multifractality in Tropical Atlantic SST Indices: Scaling-Range Artefacts and a Reappraisal of the ENSO Association
risk:new_level_sst_world.our_title: A Broken Tuning Fork: How Three Atlantic Indices Turned Out Simpler Than Thought
risk:new_level_sst_world.oneliner: Three tropical Atlantic sea surface temperature indices are monofractal, and the apparent multifractality was an artifact of choosing the wrong scale range.
risk:new_level_sst_world.why: Measures tropical Atlantic sea surface temperature indices and finds strong persistence, supporting a stayed shift rather than a spike.

risk:warmest30_t2_world.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
risk:warmest30_t2_world.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
risk:warmest30_t2_world.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
risk:warmest30_t2_world.why: Explains that record-low planetary albedo from fewer low clouds amplified the recent global temperature surge beyond known drivers.

risk:new_level_t2_world.title: Limits on CO2 Climate Forcing from Recent Temperature Data of Earth
risk:new_level_t2_world.our_title: The Tropics as a Clean Laboratory: What They Tell Us About CO2
risk:new_level_t2_world.oneliner: Satellite data from 1979–2007 show that global warming stalled in 1998, and the tropical trend matches only the weak effect of CO2 without feedbacks.
risk:new_level_t2_world.why: Uses global temperature data to show an El Nino spike can top the record without starting a new lasting level.

risk:new_level_t2_world.title: Persistence without Multifractality in Tropical Atlantic SST Indices: Scaling-Range Artefacts and a Reappraisal of the ENSO Association
risk:new_level_t2_world.our_title: A Broken Tuning Fork: How Three Atlantic Indices Turned Out Simpler Than Thought
risk:new_level_t2_world.oneliner: Three tropical Atlantic sea surface temperature indices are monofractal, and the apparent multifractality was an artifact of choosing the wrong scale range.
risk:new_level_t2_world.why: Finds tropical Atlantic sea surface temperature indices are strongly persistent, so rises tend to stay rather than reverse.

risk:new_level_t2_world.title: Basin stability and limit cycles in a conceptual model for climate tipping cascades
risk:new_level_t2_world.our_title: The Climate House of Cards: Where Does the Stability Limit Lie?
risk:new_level_t2_world.oneliner: A stability analysis of five climate systems shows that above 4°C of warming, a state with four or five tipped elements dominates, and ice sheets play a key role in Earth's stability.
risk:new_level_t2_world.why: Shows in a conceptual model that climate components can cross thresholds and settle into new stable states.

risk:models_revise_up.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
risk:models_revise_up.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
risk:models_revise_up.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
risk:models_revise_up.why: It shows models missed a record low cloud cover that amplified the 2023 heat, so forecasts can lag reality and need upward revisions.

risk:models_revise_up.title: Very early warning of a moderate-to-strong El Ni\~no in 2023
risk:models_revise_up.oneliner: Two independent methods predicted the 2023 El Niño with 89% probability and estimated its strength at 1.49±0.37°C.
risk:models_revise_up.why: It reports an early warning method that predicted the 2023 El Nino onset and strength, so model forecast shifts can be meaningful.

risk:models_below_reality.title: A Hybrid Deep-Learning Model for El Ni\~no Southern Oscillation in the Low-Data Regime
risk:models_below_reality.our_title: Navigator and Cabin Boy: How a Hybrid Model Learns to Predict El Niño from the Ocean's Short Memory
risk:models_below_reality.oneliner: A linear model steers the ship by the map, while a neural-network cabin boy learns from its mistakes, and together they predict El Niño more accurately than either alone.
risk:models_below_reality.why: It explains that scarce observations and climate model biases limit El Niño forecasts, and a hybrid model improves skill.

risk:models_below_reality.title: Using Network Theory and Machine Learning to predict El Ni\~no
risk:models_below_reality.our_title: Network Warns of El Niño a Year in Advance
risk:models_below_reality.oneliner: The ocean whispers in pairs before it screams: a new hybrid forecast catches that whisper 12 months ahead.
risk:models_below_reality.why: It shows standard El Niño forecasts lose skill after six months and that machine learning can improve that skill.

risk:models_below_reality.title: Learning Climate Variability from Scarce Data with Diffusion Models: A Test Case for ENSO
risk:models_below_reality.our_title: How a Neural Network Learns Climate from Sparse Data
risk:models_below_reality.oneliner: A diffusion model extracts the hidden structure of El Niño when observations are ten times scarcer than needed.
risk:models_below_reality.why: It shows that scarce data makes learning El Niño variability hard, but pre-training on climate models helps.

risk:ohc_2000_record.title: The Rise and Fall of ENSO in a Warming World: Insights from a Lag-Linear Model
risk:ohc_2000_record.our_title: The El Niño Pendulum: How Warming First Amplifies, Then Damps It
risk:ohc_2000_record.oneliner: A simple delayed model explains why El Niño strengthens at first and then weakens under global warming, and lets you forecast its strength without running climate models.
risk:ohc_2000_record.why: Explains how a warmer upper ocean and stronger layering can strengthen El Nino, so a record hot ocean may mean forecasts see a different system.

risk:layers_lag.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
risk:layers_lag.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
risk:layers_lag.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
risk:layers_lag.why: It cautions that record-low planetary albedo amplified the 2023 global temperature surge, so other factors can shift the peak warmth.

risk:global_next_year.title: Impact of natural disasters on consumer behavior: case of the 2017 El Nino phenomenon in Peru
risk:global_next_year.our_title: A City's Pulse After a Natural Disaster
risk:global_next_year.oneliner: Bank transactions from six million Peruvians reveal how the 2017 El Niño shifted shopping habits and how quickly Lima's economy bounced back.
risk:global_next_year.why: Bank card data from Peru show El Nino shifted consumer spending and marked a recovery time, matching delayed economic impacts.

risk:global_next_year.title: Very early warning of a moderate-to-strong El Ni\~no in 2023
risk:global_next_year.oneliner: Two independent methods predicted the 2023 El Niño with 89% probability and estimated its strength at 1.49±0.37°C.
risk:global_next_year.why: Explains that El Nino adds about 0.2 degrees Celsius to global air temperature, so the hottest year comes after onset.

risk:global_next_year.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
risk:global_next_year.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
risk:global_next_year.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
risk:global_next_year.why: Caveat: low cloud cover also helped cause the 2023 heat spike, so ocean heat is not the only driver.

alert:the_share_of_models_below_reality_.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
alert:the_share_of_models_below_reality_.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
alert:the_share_of_models_below_reality_.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
alert:the_share_of_models_below_reality_.why: Finds 2023 warming beat model estimates by 0.2 K and links the gap to record low planetary albedo.

alert:the_share_of_models_below_reality_.title: Recent Weakening of the Global Radiative Feedback
alert:the_share_of_models_below_reality_.our_title: The Climate Has Become Worse at Shedding Heat
alert:the_share_of_models_below_reality_.oneliner: Over the past thirty years, Earth has become less efficient at radiating excess heat into space.
alert:the_share_of_models_below_reality_.why: Shows global radiative feedback weakened recently, making observed warming stronger than many models assume.

alert:12_of_26_forecast_models_are_broke.title: Sensitivity of Indian summer monsoon rainfall forecast skill of CFSv2 model to initial conditions and the role of model biases
alert:12_of_26_forecast_models_are_broke.our_title: Why the February Monsoon Forecast Is Deceptively Accurate
alert:12_of_26_forecast_models_are_broke.oneliner: The CFSv2 model shows better skill for Indian monsoon forecasts starting in February, but the success is a fluke caused by a wrong La Niña prediction in 1983.
alert:12_of_26_forecast_models_are_broke.why: Shows CFSv2 made a correct monsoon forecast for the wrong physical reason, so a model can score well yet still be biased.

alert:12_of_26_forecast_models_are_broke.title: Unraveling the mystery of tropical monsoon long-term prediction
alert:12_of_26_forecast_models_are_broke.our_title: Network catches the monsoon beyond the horizon
alert:12_of_26_forecast_models_are_broke.oneliner: A global web of temperature links predicts rains in four tropical regions 4–10 months ahead more accurately than seasonal models.
alert:12_of_26_forecast_models_are_broke.why: Reports a network model outperforming CFSv2 and SEAS5, supporting that existing seasonal forecast systems can underperform.

alert:in_the_jun_2026_issue_15_of_24_mod.title: Climate network and complexity based ENSO forecast for 2026
alert:in_the_jun_2026_issue_15_of_24_mod.our_title: El Niño 2026: Two Barometers, One Forecast
alert:in_the_jun_2026_issue_15_of_24_mod.oneliner: Two independent methods gave conflicting forecasts for 2026, so the authors combined them into a probabilistic outlook.
alert:in_the_jun_2026_issue_15_of_24_mod.why: It gives a separate 2026 ENSO forecast that also expected neutral or a weak event, illustrating forecasts undershot the observed ONI.

region:west_africa.title: Impact of dynamical regionalization on precipitation biases and teleconnections over West Africa
region:west_africa.our_title: Monsoon under the Magnifying Glass: How Regional Models Change Rainfall Forecasts over West Africa
region:west_africa.oneliner: Regional climate models improve some monsoon-ocean connections and degrade others.
region:west_africa.why: Model biases in the West African monsoon and its ENSO teleconnection help explain the weak mixed rainfall signal.

region:europe.title: CNN-based forecasting of early winter NAO using sea surface temperature
region:europe.our_title: The Ocean Whispers Early: Neural Network Hears the Atlantic Winter Three Months Ahead
region:europe.oneliner: A convolutional neural network reads sea surface temperatures and predicts the European winter more accurately than linear models.
region:europe.why: Shows early winter El Nino can nudge the North Atlantic Oscillation positive and late winter negative, while models struggle with this link.

region:sahel.title: Oceanic Forcing on Interannual Variability of Sahel Heavy and Moderate Daily Rainfall
region:sahel.our_title: The Ocean Dictates the Rains of the Sahel
region:sahel.oneliner: Warm waters in the Atlantic and Mediterranean drive moderate downpours, while the Pacific Ocean, via La Niña, amplifies extreme storms.
region:sahel.why: Shows that El Niño weakens Sahel summer rainfall mainly by cutting heavy daily rain events, the main source of year-to-year variability.

region:sahel.title: Climate, Crops, and Postharvest Conflict
region:sahel.oneliner: El Niño shifts political violence in African farming regions right after harvest.
region:sahel.why: Finds in Sahel croplands that El Niño tends to reduce harvest-time political violence while La Niña increases it, adding nuance to conflict risk.

region:north_africa_levant.title: Spatial Analysis of Seasonal Precipitation over Iran: Co-Variation with Climate Indices
region:north_africa_levant.our_title: Three Oceanic Conductors Control Iran's Rains
region:north_africa_levant.oneliner: Three climate indices explain where and how much Iran's seasonal rainfall deviates from the norm.
region:north_africa_levant.why: Maps Iran's seasonal precipitation response to ENSO, PDO and NAO, showing winter is most affected.

region:russia_centralasia.title: Predictability of warm and cold winters: Assessment of El Niño effects in the North Eurasian regions
region:russia_centralasia.our_title: El Niño as Conductor: Why Winters in Transbaikalia Don't Follow the Pacific
region:russia_centralasia.oneliner: A warm or cold phase in the equatorial Pacific hints in advance what winter will be like in different regions of Russia: mild, harsh, or utterly unpredictable.
region:russia_centralasia.why: Assesses El Niño effects on warm and cold winters in northern Eurasia, supporting the mild European Russia tendency and its limits.

region:pacific_islands.title: Differential imprints of distinct ENSO flavors in global patterns of very low and high seasonal precipitation
region:pacific_islands.our_title: Two Faces of El Niño: How Different Patterns of Ocean Heat Rewrite the Map of Droughts and Floods
region:pacific_islands.oneliner: Eastern Pacific and Central Pacific types of El Niño and La Niña affect global precipitation differently, and this is only visible in the statistics of coincidences of rare events.
region:pacific_islands.why: Measures how Eastern Pacific El Niño raises the odds of very dry western and wet central Pacific seasons.

region:pacific_islands.title: Forecasting the El Ni\~no type well before the spring predictability barrier
region:pacific_islands.our_title: El Niño type can be predicted a year before the spring barrier
region:pacific_islands.oneliner: The difference in ocean surface temperature between the western and central Pacific in December indicates whether the next El Niño will be eastern or central.
region:pacific_islands.why: Explains that El Niño type (east or central Pacific warming) switches which Pacific islands get dry or wet.

region:southern_cone.title: Solar Forcing of the Streamflow of a Continental Scale South American River
region:southern_cone.oneliner: For a century, the flow of South America's largest river has followed the rhythm of solar activity.
region:southern_cone.why: Links Paraná streamflow variability to solar cycles and El Niño, which can help explain flood risk in the basin.

term:nino34.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:nino34.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:nino34.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:nino34.why: Develops a method to estimate the baseline averages used for Niño 3.4 temperature anomalies, relevant under climate change.

term:nino34.title: Forecasting the magnitude and onset of El Nino based on climate network
term:nino34.our_title: El Niño: Predicting Strength and Onset a Year in Advance
term:nino34.oneliner: A climate network in the Niño 3.4 region predicts the onset and strength of El Niño about a year ahead.
term:nino34.why: Forecasts El Niño onset and magnitude from temperature anomaly patterns inside Niño 3.4, showing its predictive value.

region:andes_peru.title: Differential imprints of distinct ENSO flavors in global patterns of very low and high seasonal precipitation
region:andes_peru.our_title: Two Faces of El Niño: How Different Patterns of Ocean Heat Rewrite the Map of Droughts and Floods
region:andes_peru.oneliner: Eastern Pacific and Central Pacific types of El Niño and La Niña affect global precipitation differently, and this is only visible in the statistics of coincidences of rare events.
region:andes_peru.why: Shows eastern Pacific El Niño events bring very high or low seasonal rain over wider areas than central Pacific events, matching stronger coastal impacts.

region:andes_peru.title: Impact of natural disasters on consumer behavior: case of the 2017 El Nino phenomenon in Peru
region:andes_peru.our_title: A City's Pulse After a Natural Disaster
region:andes_peru.oneliner: Bank transactions from six million Peruvians reveal how the 2017 El Niño shifted shopping habits and how quickly Lima's economy bounced back.
region:andes_peru.why: Uses card transaction data from the 2017 El Niño in Peru to measure how floods changed spending and which merchants were affected.

term:lanina.title: Climate network suggests enhanced El Ni\~no global impacts in localized areas
term:lanina.our_title: Climate Network: How El Niño Tightens Its Grip and Strikes with Precision
term:lanina.oneliner: A directed climate network shows that during El Niño and La Niña, the planet-wide impact becomes stronger but is concentrated in smaller areas.
term:lanina.why: Measures where El Niño and La Niña make regions warmer or cooler, supporting mirrored weather effects.

term:lanina.title: Spatio-temporal Patterns between ENSO and Weather-related Power Outages in the Continental United States
term:lanina.our_title: The Ocean Conducts Blackouts: How La Niña Steers the US Power Grid
term:lanina.oneliner: La Niña raises the number of weather-related power outages in the US, and by century's end, heat could increase them 26-fold.
term:lanina.why: Finds La Niña phases raise weather-related power outages in the US, showing its weather impacts.

term:elnino.title: Intrinsic unpredictability of strong El Ni\~no events
term:elnino.our_title: The Pacific Ocean Pendulum: Why Strong El Niños Are Unpredictable
term:elnino.oneliner: The ocean behaves like a pendulum that sometimes swings to huge amplitudes and sometimes gets stuck in small oscillations, and the switch between these regimes cannot be predicted.
term:elnino.why: Shows strong El Nino events can be unpredictably strong, though they peak in northern winter and affect global weather.

term:elnino.title: Intra-annual Principal Modes and Evolution Mechanism of the El Nino Southern Oscillation
term:elnino.our_title: Tug-of-War in the Tropics: How Seasonal Air Oscillations Drive El Niño
term:elnino.oneliner: Two dominant intra-annual modes of tropical air temperature are closely tied to the phases of El Niño and La Niña.
term:elnino.why: Explains how links between air temperature patterns make El Nino grow and then decay after northern winter, so events last about a year.

term:elnino.title: Climate Networks around the Globe are Significantly Effected by El Nino
term:elnino.our_title: Climate Networks: How El Niño Snaps Invisible Threads
term:elnino.oneliner: El Niño barely changes average temperatures, but it destroys the connections between distant points on the planet.
term:elnino.why: Measures how El Nino breaks many links in a global climate network, supporting the claim that it changes weather on half the planet.

term:nino4.title: Forecasting the El Ni\~no type well before the spring predictability barrier
term:nino4.our_title: El Niño type can be predicted a year before the spring barrier
term:nino4.oneliner: The difference in ocean surface temperature between the western and central Pacific in December indicates whether the next El Niño will be eastern or central.
term:nino4.why: Explains that zonal sea surface temperature differences in the tropical Pacific can indicate whether an El Niño is central or eastern Pacific type.

term:oni.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:oni.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:oni.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:oni.why: It shows standard 30-year normals for Niño 3.4 can be biased under warming, so ONI anomalies may need adjusted baselines.

term:type.title: Differential imprints of distinct ENSO flavors in global patterns of very low and high seasonal precipitation
term:type.our_title: Two Faces of El Niño: How Different Patterns of Ocean Heat Rewrite the Map of Droughts and Floods
term:type.oneliner: Eastern Pacific and Central Pacific types of El Niño and La Niña affect global precipitation differently, and this is only visible in the statistics of coincidences of rare events.
term:type.why: Shows eastern Pacific events produce broader precipitation anomalies than central Pacific events, so their impacts differ.

term:type.title: Forecasting the El Ni\~no type well before the spring predictability barrier
term:type.our_title: El Niño type can be predicted a year before the spring barrier
term:type.oneliner: The difference in ocean surface temperature between the western and central Pacific in December indicates whether the next El Niño will be eastern or central.
term:type.why: Shows eastern and central Pacific El Niño types can be separated early and that their regional rainfall impacts differ.

term:anomaly.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:anomaly.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:anomaly.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:anomaly.why: Explains climate normals as multi-decade averages and anomalies as departures from them, the same concept used for 1991-2020.

term:trend.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:trend.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:trend.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:trend.why: Proposes a real-time filter for climate normals and anomalies that accounts for warming trends, improving above-trend anomaly estimates.

term:soi.title: Long-term non-linear predictability of ENSO events over the 20th century
term:soi.our_title: A Map That Could Have Predicted El Niño
term:soi.oneliner: The Southern Oscillation Index holds enough information to forecast El Niño events two to four years ahead.
term:soi.why: Shows the long SOI record contains enough signal to predict ENSO years ahead, supporting its use as an atmospheric ENSO index.

term:analog.title: A Nonanticipative Analog Method for Long-Term Forecasting of Air Temperature Extremes
term:analog.our_title: How to Predict Heat a Year in Advance
term:analog.oneliner: A non-lookahead analog method predicts extreme temperatures with 100% sign accuracy.
term:analog.why: Demonstrates a nonanticipative analog method for forecasting temperature extremes from past observations, no climate model.

term:dynstat.title: Knowledge-based Deep Learning for Modeling Chaotic Systems
term:dynstat.our_title: Taming Chaos with Physics: Predicting Extreme Events from Sparse Data
term:dynstat.oneliner: A hybrid neural network trained on synthetic data and physical laws predicts extreme events more accurately when data are scarce.
term:dynstat.why: Deep learning for extreme events often lacks enough historical data, so it adds physics and simulated data to cope.

term:dynstat.title: Hierarchical Testing of a Hybrid Machine Learning-Physics Global Atmosphere Model
term:dynstat.our_title: A Student Who Learned Physics from a Textbook
term:dynstat.oneliner: The hybrid atmospheric model NeuralGCM passes an exam on cyclones, El Niño, and anomalous warming, but stumbles in the stratosphere.
term:dynstat.why: A hybrid ML-physics model reproduces ENSO teleconnections but shows deficiencies in nonlinear response and under out-of-distribution warming.

term:lead.title: Using Network Theory and Machine Learning to predict El Ni\~no
term:lead.our_title: Network Warns of El Niño a Year in Advance
term:lead.oneliner: The ocean whispers in pairs before it screams: a new hybrid forecast catches that whisper 12 months ahead.
term:lead.why: Shows ENSO forecast skill normally falls beyond six months, the basis for treating lead 6 errors as expected.

term:lead.title: Entropic learning enables skilful forecasts of ENSO phase at up to two years lead time
term:lead.our_title: Council of Sages: How Entropy Predicts El Niño Two Years Ahead
term:lead.oneliner: An ensemble of entropy-based models, trained solely on satellite data, forecasts the El Niño phase up to 24 months ahead with skill comparable to the best dynamical systems.
term:lead.why: Measures ENSO phase skill out to 22-24 months, showing lead 6 is not a hard limit for all models.

term:wwv.title: The Rise and Fall of ENSO in a Warming World: Insights from a Lag-Linear Model
term:wwv.our_title: The El Niño Pendulum: How Warming First Amplifies, Then Damps It
term:wwv.oneliner: A simple delayed model explains why El Niño strengthens at first and then weakens under global warming, and lets you forecast its strength without running climate models.
term:wwv.why: Shows subsurface heat leads surface warming, supporting the fuel gauge idea.

term:t300.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:t300.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:t300.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:t300.why: Explains how climate normals and anomalies are estimated, and warns standard baselines can be biased in a changing climate.

term:teleconnection.title: The link between North Atlantic tropical cyclones and ENSO in seasonal forecasts
term:teleconnection.our_title: The Overzealous Translator: Why Models Overestimate the El Niño–Hurricane Link
term:teleconnection.oneliner: Six European seasonal forecast models overestimate the strength of the El Niño–Atlantic hurricane connection, especially in the Caribbean basin.
term:teleconnection.why: Shows seasonal forecast models capture the ENSO to Atlantic hurricane link but overstate it, meaning it is statistical not deterministic.

term:teleconnection.title: Global teleconnectivity structures of the El Ni\~no-Southern Oscillation and large volcanic eruptions -- An evolving network perspective
term:teleconnection.our_title: The Global Climate Web: How El Niño and Volcanoes Rewire Temperature Connections
term:teleconnection.oneliner: A climate network shows El Niño shattering the global temperature hierarchy, while volcanoes act more locally.
term:teleconnection.why: Finds El Nino phases produce episodic breakdowns and strong teleconnections, supporting the usual not guaranteed framing.

term:teleconnection.title: Metastability, atmospheric midlatitude circulation regimes and large-scale teleconnection: a data-driven approach
term:teleconnection.our_title: Rooms of the Winter Sky: How the Atmosphere Chooses the Weather
term:teleconnection.oneliner: In winter, the Northern Hemisphere's atmosphere can spend weeks in one of four 'rooms'—stable circulation regimes—and the transitions between them follow hidden rules.
term:teleconnection.why: Links recurring mid latitude circulation patterns to teleconnections, showing the atmospheric rearrangement behind remote links.

term:u850.title: Rotational and Irrotational Wind Forcing as dual drivers of El Nino Southern Oscillation variability
term:u850.our_title: Twin Winds: How Rotation and Divergence Drive El Niño
term:u850.oneliner: One part of the wind drives fast climate swings, the other drives slow decadal waves.
term:u850.why: Shows how equatorial wind stress shifts the ocean's warm layer, supporting the idea that trades are an engine of ENSO.

term:shout.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:shout.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:shout.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:shout.why: Explains how seasonal baselines for Niño 3.4 are estimated and warns that standard 30-year normals can be biased under climate change.

term:tlt.title: Comment on "Influence of the Southern Oscillation on tropospheric temperature" by J. D. McLean, C. R. de Freitas, and R. M. Carter
term:tlt.our_title: El Niño as a Thermostat: The Accumulated Effect of the Southern Oscillation
term:tlt.oneliner: The cumulative Southern Oscillation Index explains half of tropospheric warming since 1960, challenging the dominant role of greenhouse gases.
term:tlt.why: It finds a running total of El Nino and La Nina explains about half of tropospheric temperature variation, matching delayed ocean heating.

term:pinksheet.title: Climate, Crops, and Postharvest Conflict
term:pinksheet.oneliner: El Niño shifts political violence in African farming regions right after harvest.
term:pinksheet.why: Shows El Nino shocks during the crop growing season change harvest related conflict only in exposed croplands, so impacts are local and seasonal.

term:pinksheet.title: Differential imprints of distinct ENSO flavors in global patterns of very low and high seasonal precipitation
term:pinksheet.our_title: Two Faces of El Niño: How Different Patterns of Ocean Heat Rewrite the Map of Droughts and Floods
term:pinksheet.oneliner: Eastern Pacific and Central Pacific types of El Niño and La Niña affect global precipitation differently, and this is only visible in the statistics of coincidences of rare events.
term:pinksheet.why: Maps how different El Nino types bring very low or high seasonal rainfall to particular regions, shaping agricultural production there.

term:pinksheet.title: Climate network suggests enhanced El Ni\~no global impacts in localized areas
term:pinksheet.our_title: Climate Network: How El Niño Tightens Its Grip and Strikes with Precision
term:pinksheet.oneliner: A directed climate network shows that during El Niño and La Niña, the planet-wide impact becomes stronger but is concentrated in smaller areas.
term:pinksheet.why: Finds El Nino temperature links are concentrated in limited areas and much of the globe is unaffected, so impacts are localized.

term:coupling.title: Modelling the coupling between ocean and atmosphere; the global signature of the El Ni\~no/La Ni\~na Southern Oscillation
term:coupling.our_title: The Planet's Pulse with an Irregular Rhythm
term:coupling.oneliner: Analysis of long-term El Niño index records reveals power laws and long memory that models miss.
term:coupling.why: Models the ocean atmosphere coupling that gives ENSO its global climate signature and distant impacts.

term:coupling.title: Redefining climate index with sea surface temperature of key area can better express atmospheric physical activity
term:coupling.our_title: An Ocean Thermometer Instead of a Barometer: A New Take on Climate Indices
term:coupling.oneliner: Redefining climate indices through sea surface temperature differences sharply strengthens their link to river runoff and points to a common astronomical driver.
term:coupling.why: Questions the standard SOI pressure index and suggests sea surface temperature differences capture atmospheric response better.

term:coupling.title: Coupled Ocean-Atmosphere Dynamics in a Machine Learning Earth System Model
term:coupling.our_title: Ocean and Atmosphere Learn to Speak the Same Language
term:coupling.oneliner: The neural network model Ola reproduces El Niño for the first time by modeling the ocean and atmosphere as a single system.
term:coupling.why: Shows a machine learning model reproduces coupled ocean atmosphere dynamics including El Nino, supporting the link.

term:ersst.title: Probabilistic reconstruction of global sea surface temperature using generative diffusion models
term:ersst.our_title: The Ocean as a Draft: Diffusion Model Reveals All Possible Temperatures
term:ersst.oneliner: The SAGE neural network turns sparse measurements into a full fan of plausible ocean temperature maps, honestly showing where confidence is high and where it is nearly zero.
term:ersst.why: Explains that standard deterministic SST reconstructions like ERSST may understate observation uncertainty; offers a probabilistic alternative.

term:pmel.title: The Rise and Fall of ENSO in a Warming World: Insights from a Lag-Linear Model
term:pmel.our_title: The El Niño Pendulum: How Warming First Amplifies, Then Damps It
term:pmel.oneliner: A simple delayed model explains why El Niño strengthens at first and then weakens under global warming, and lets you forecast its strength without running climate models.
term:pmel.why: In model projections, subsurface warming is linked to later surface warming, supporting the idea that El Nino heat builds below first.

term:uah.title: Temperature variability over the Po Valley, Italy, according to radiosounding data
term:uah.our_title: The Po Valley Air Orchestra: How Global Rhythms Conduct Temperatures Up to 20 Kilometers
term:uah.oneliner: 22 years of radiosonde measurements over the Po Valley show that about 70% of temperature variability at all heights up to 20 km is driven by waves with periods from one month to seven years, linked to global atmospheric oscillations.
term:uah.why: Radiosonde profiles over Italy show temperature oscillations change phase with height and vary by layer, backing the whole air column view.

term:wwb.title: An improved noise model for representing westerly wind bursts in the recharge oscillator model of ENSO
term:wwb.our_title: The Noise That Rocks the Pacific Swing
term:wwb.oneliner: Bursts of westerly wind act like random pushes, and a new noise model explains why there are more of them before a big El Niño.
term:wwb.why: Models westerly wind bursts as noise that amplifies El Niño, with stronger events having more bursts.

term:wwb.title: On the Estimation of Climate Normals and Anomalies
term:wwb.our_title: Climate Norms Under Pressure from Trends
term:wwb.oneliner: A new filter estimates climate norms in real time, accounting for trend and seasonality, and shows where standard 30-year averages fail.
term:wwb.why: Proposes a real time filter for wind anomalies, useful background for the two sigma threshold.

term:eei.title: Recent global temperature surge amplified by record-low planetary albedo
term:eei.our_title: Earth Took Off Its Sunglasses: Why 2023 Was Anomalously Hot
term:eei.oneliner: In 2023, the planet absorbed more sunlight than in any year in the past 80 years, and it was this, not El Niño, that accounted for nearly all of the unexplained temperature jump.
term:eei.why: Finds record low planetary albedo from fewer low clouds boosted absorbed sunlight, helping explain the recent jump in Earth's energy imbalance.

term:iod.title: Indo-Pacific variability on seasonal to multidecadal timescales. Part II: Multiscale atmosphere-ocean linkages
term:iod.our_title: An Orchestra Without a Conductor: How the Ocean and Atmosphere Strike a Deal
term:iod.oneliner: A 1,300-year model run shows that slow temperature swings in the western Pacific control the strength of El Niño and monsoons.
term:iod.why: Shows how El Nino wind patterns can create the sea surface temperature pattern of an Indian Ocean Dipole.

term:iod.title: Coupling functions in climate
term:iod.our_title: Seasonal Climate Seesaw: How El Niño and the Indian Ocean Dipole Are Linked
term:iod.oneliner: A two-dimensional stochastic model with coupling functions shows that El Niño drives the seasonal variability of the Indian Ocean Dipole, not the other way around.
term:iod.why: Quantifies how El Nino controls the Indian Ocean Dipole, mainly at its peak.

term:iod.title: On the all-India rainfall index and sub-India rainfall heterogeneity
term:iod.our_title: Monsoon Season: How a Single Index Captures India's Mosaic
term:iod.oneliner: The all-India rainfall index reflects not the average intensity of downpours but the area they cover.
term:iod.why: Finds the Indian Ocean Dipole influence on Indian rainfall becomes clearer once El Nino is removed.

term:mjo.title: A Simple Intermediate Coupled MJO-ENSO Model: Multiscale Interactions and ENSO Complexity
term:mjo.our_title: A Bridge Between Typhoon and Current: How El Niño Is Born
term:mjo.oneliner: A simple model connects fast wind bursts, multi-year ocean rhythms, and decadal shifts, reproducing the full diversity of El Niño.
term:mjo.why: Models how MJO wind forcing can trigger ENSO events, supporting the idea that the MJO times the pushes.

term:mjo.title: A Stochastic Conceptual Model for the Coupled ENSO and MJO
term:mjo.our_title: A Bridge Between Ocean and Atmosphere Rhythms
term:mjo.oneliner: A simple model links the two major tropical oscillations and reproduces their statistics.
term:mjo.why: Uses a stochastic model to capture interactions between wind, MJO and ENSO, adding evidence for the coupling.

term:mei.title: Quantifying the Multivariate ENSO Index (MEI) coupling to CO2 concentration and to the length of day variations
term:mei.our_title: El Niño as Conductor: How Climate Ties Together Earth's Rotation and Carbon Dioxide
term:mei.oneliner: Extreme values of the El Niño index are synchronously linked to changes in CO₂ concentration and day length.
term:mei.why: Quantifies how MEI links multiple tropical Pacific variables and tracks coupled variability.

block:food.title: Climate, Crops, and Postharvest Conflict
block:food.oneliner: El Niño shifts political violence in African farming regions right after harvest.
block:food.why: Measures how ENSO crop-growing-season shocks change postharvest conflict in exposed croplands, strongest in Southern Africa and the Sahel.

block:type.title: Differential imprints of distinct ENSO flavors in global patterns of very low and high seasonal precipitation
block:type.our_title: Two Faces of El Niño: How Different Patterns of Ocean Heat Rewrite the Map of Droughts and Floods
block:type.oneliner: Eastern Pacific and Central Pacific types of El Niño and La Niña affect global precipitation differently, and this is only visible in the statistics of coincidences of rare events.
block:type.why: Shows EP and CP El Niños leave different footprints in extreme seasonal rainfall, with EP affecting larger areas.

block:type.title: Forecasting the El Ni\~no type well before the spring predictability barrier
block:type.our_title: El Niño type can be predicted a year before the spring barrier
block:type.oneliner: The difference in ocean surface temperature between the western and central Pacific in December indicates whether the next El Niño will be eastern or central.
block:type.why: Finds the east-west Pacific temperature contrast signals whether an upcoming El Niño will be Eastern or Central Pacific.

block:type.title: A Multiscale Model for El Ni\~no Complexity
block:type.our_title: Three Rhythms of El Niño: A Model of Complexity
block:type.oneliner: A three-region stochastic model explains the diversity of El Niño by unifying intraseasonal, interannual, and decadal processes.
block:type.why: Shows how Central and Eastern Pacific El Niño patterns can arise from combined intraseasonal, interannual and decadal processes.

block:peak.title: (Un)predictability of strong El Ni\~no events
block:peak.our_title: The Pendulum That Forgets How to Swing
block:peak.oneliner: Strong El Niños can vanish for decades because the climate system flips between two distinct modes of oscillation.
block:peak.why: Uses a simple El Niño model to show weak forcing can cause irregular switching that limits strong event predictability.

block:models.title: (Un)predictability of strong El Ni\~no events
block:models.our_title: The Pendulum That Forgets How to Swing
block:models.oneliner: Strong El Niños can vanish for decades because the climate system flips between two distinct modes of oscillation.
block:models.why: Finds an intrinsic predictability limit for strong El Niño events from irregular switching between oscillatory and chaotic states.

block:models.title: Discovery of a Phenomenological Dynamical Model for Predicting the El Ni\~no-Southern Oscillation
block:models.our_title: A Trail in the Sand: How 135 Years of Weather Yielded the El Niño Equation
block:models.oneliner: From a single long observational record, researchers extracted a simple nonlinear equation that predicts El Niño better than supercomputer models.
block:models.why: Shows model skill is limited by missing ENSO nonlinearity, and a nonlinear model from observations improves prediction and reduces the spring predictability barrier.

block:models.title: A Hybrid Deep-Learning Model for El Ni\~no Southern Oscillation in the Low-Data Regime
block:models.our_title: Navigator and Cabin Boy: How a Hybrid Model Learns to Predict El Niño from the Ocean's Short Memory
block:models.oneliner: A linear model steers the ship by the map, while a neural-network cabin boy learns from its mistakes, and together they predict El Niño more accurately than either alone.
block:models.why: Notes climate model biases and linear models missing warm-cold asymmetry, and a hybrid model capturing that asymmetry improves ENSO forecasts.

note: vector finds what is about the same thing; the model decides whether it belongs next to the statement. A link means 'this is what the research says about this', not 'this is the source of that number'.
